question: An 18-year-old woman comes to the physician because of worsening headache and exertional dyspnea for 6 days. Two months ago, she had a spontaneous abortion. Since then, she has had intermittent bloody vaginal discharge. Pelvic examination shows blood at the cervical os and a tender, mildly enlarged uterus. A urine pregnancy test is positive. An x-ray of the chest shows multiple round opacities in both lungs. Dilation and curettage is performed. Histopathology of the curettage specimen is most likely to show which of the following findings?

options.opa: Whorled pattern of smooth muscle fibers surrounded by a pseudocapsule
options.opb: Poorly differentiated glandular cells with myometrial invasion
options.opc: Cytotrophoblasts and syncytiotrophoblasts without chorionic villi
options.opd: Glomeruli-like central blood vessels enveloped by germ cells
options.ope: Trophoblast hyperplasia with mixture of edematous and normal villi

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Positive urine pregnancy test -> Spontaneous abortion two months ago -> Intermittent bloody vaginal discharge -> Pelvic examination findings of blood at cervical os and tender, mildly enlarged uterus -> Dilation and curettage performed -> Histopathology likely to show trophoblast hyperplasia with a mixture of edematous and normal villi -> 85%

analysis: The clinical presentation of a positive urine pregnancy test, worsening headache, exertional dyspnea, intermittent bloody vaginal discharge, and multiple round opacities in both lungs on chest x-ray suggests a diagnosis of gestational trophoblastic disease, specifically choriocarcinoma. The histopathology findings of cytology consistent with choriocarcinoma would show cytotrophoblasts and syncytiotrophoblasts without chorionic villi.
